evals.prompt: We have an English-only Umbraco 17.5 site (Razor views, en-US is the only language). We're launching in Denmark next month and need every page available in Danish too, on the same domain as example.com/da, with English at example.com/en. Editors should be able to leave a Danish field blank and have English show instead. We also need a language switcher in the header and proper hreflang tags for SEO. Set it up.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds da-DK as a language with fallback to en-US, enables vary by culture on the Document Types (keeping shared values invariant), configures Culture and Hostnames on the site root with a domain per culture, renders values with Fallback.ToLanguage, and adds the skill's language switcher and hreflang partials, explaining what the package import cannot do.
expectations: The agent adds da-DK as a language and sets its fallback language to en-US (or explains exactly where to set it)
The agent explains that importing languages from a package manifest does not set fallback, mandatory or default, and that those must be configured separately
The agent enables 'Allow vary by culture' on the relevant Document Types and advises keeping values that are the same in every language (e.g. SKUs, dates) as shared/invariant properties
The agent configures a domain per culture on the site root via Culture and Hostnames (e.g. example.com/en → en-US and example.com/da → da-DK, or relative /en and /da)
Blank Danish values fall back to English via Fallback.ToLanguage (or equivalent), not via a `??` on Value<string>, which never fires because blank values are empty strings

The language switcher links to the current page in other published cultures, compares cultures without ToLower() (case-insensitive comparison), and handles a missing home node or untranslated page without throwing
hreflang is emitted as <link rel="alternate" hreflang> in <head> with absolute URLs and an x-default, not only as an attribute on switcher links
The agent prefers the Umbraco Developer MCP for backoffice steps and otherwise walks through them manually, rather than skipping them
If no buildable Umbraco project is available, the agent does not falsely claim to have built or verified the site

evals.prompt: Our Umbraco 17 site has English and German. Pages render German correctly at /de/, but a JSON endpoint in our custom API controller that returns the page title always returns the English title even when called from the German site with ?culture=de-DE. Same problem in a nightly Hangfire job that builds a German product feed. Why, and how do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that outside a routed front-end request no variation context is set, so IPublishedContent resolves to the default language, and fixes it by setting IVariationContextAccessor.VariationContext = new VariationContext(culture) or passing the culture to Value/Url explicitly.
expectations: The agent explains that API controllers and background jobs are culture-less contexts where IPublishedContent resolves to the default language
The fix sets IVariationContextAccessor.VariationContext to a new VariationContext(culture), or passes the culture explicitly to Value(alias, culture) / Url(culture)
The culture comes from the request or job input (e.g. the culture parameter), not a hardcoded culture list
The agent does not suggest changing Umbraco:CMS:Global:DefaultUILanguage or the default language as the fix
The agent does not lowercase the culture code (e.g. keeps de-DE, compares case-insensitively)
If no buildable Umbraco project is available, the agent does not falsely claim to have verified the fix

evals.prompt: We're scripting our Danish launch on Umbraco 17 so it's repeatable across environments. A teammate wrote a package migration that imports a package.xml containing our da-DK language and about 40 dictionary items (the Danish values use LanguageCultureAlias="da-dk"). A startup job then sets the Danish property values on our existing, already-published English pages and calls IContentPublishingService.PublishBranchAsync(rootKey, ["*"], PublishBranchFilter.IncludeUnpublished, userKey, false). For the Danish launch they also set Umbraco:CMS:Global:DefaultUILanguage to "da-DK" in appsettings.json. After deploying: every dictionary item only has English, the Danish page edits never go live, templates using Fallback.ToLanguage show nothing for blank Danish fields instead of English, and the site's default language is still English. What went wrong and how do we fix each problem?
evals.expected_output: The agent diagnoses four separate causes: the package's lowercase LanguageCultureAlias is matched case-sensitively so the Danish dictionary values are silently dropped; a branch publish with "*" on already-published variant nodes republishes only the default culture; package import never sets a language's fallback so Fallback.ToLanguage has nothing to fall back to; and DefaultUILanguage is the backoffice UI language, not the content default language. It fixes each without lowercasing cultures.
expectations: The agent explains the Danish dictionary values were dropped because LanguageCultureAlias is matched case-sensitively against the installed language's ISO code, so "da-dk" doesn't match "da-DK", and fixes it by using the exact ISO casing "da-DK"

The agent explains that PublishBranchAsync with ["*"] on already-published variant nodes republishes only the default culture, and fixes it by passing explicit cultures (e.g. ["en-US", "da-DK"]) or each node's cultures

The agent explains that importing a language from a package does not set its fallback language, and fixes it by setting da-DK's fallback to English (backoffice Settings → Languages, MCP, or ILanguageService/FallbackIsoCode in the migration)

The agent explains that Umbraco:CMS:Global:DefaultUILanguage is the backoffice UI language, not the site's default content language, which is set on the language itself (and questions whether Danish should really become the default)
The agent does not propose lowercasing cultures or comparing them with ToLower() as a fix
If no buildable Umbraco project is available, the agent does not falsely claim to have run the migration or verified the fixes

evals.prompt: Our Umbraco 17 install is headless: a Next.js front end reads everything from the Content Delivery API. We've added French as a second language and translated the content in the backoffice. How does the Next.js app get the French versions, and how should we handle the language switcher and hreflang?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that the Delivery API selects the variant via the Accept-Language header, that the front end should carry the language in its own routing and send it on every call, and that the switcher and hreflang tags are built in the front end from the cultures the item is published in, rather than using Razor partials.
expectations: The agent explains the Delivery API returns the French variant when the request sends Accept-Language: fr-FR (or the site's French ISO code)
The agent recommends carrying the language in the front end's routing (e.g. /[lang]/...) and sending that culture on every Delivery API call
The agent says the switcher and hreflang are built in the Next.js app, and does not tell the user to add Razor partials to a headless site
The agent notes that only cultures the item is published in should be linked in the switcher or hreflang
If no buildable project is available, the agent does not falsely claim to have run the front end or the API

evals.prompt: We need to add Chinese (Hong Kong), zh-HK, as a content language on our Umbraco 17.5 site running on Linux, but it doesn't appear in the dropdown under Settings → Languages → Create. What's going on and how do we fix it?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that under ICU a valid culture can be missing from the dropdown either because GetCultures doesn't enumerate it or because it is flagged UserCustomCulture and rejected by IIsoCodeValidator, and fixes it with a composer that replaces ICultureService (and IIsoCodeValidator where the culture is rejected) — e.g. the documented composer — with the caveat that a replaced validator affects all culture validation.
expectations: The agent explains that zh-HK is missing because under ICU it is either not enumerated by CultureInfo.GetCultures or flagged as a user custom culture and rejected by Umbraco's IIsoCodeValidator

The agent adds a composer that replaces ICultureService (via AddUnique or equivalent) so zh-HK is listed, and also replaces IIsoCodeValidator only where the culture would otherwise be rejected — the official docs' composer (replacing both) is acceptable

If the agent replaces IIsoCodeValidator, it warns that the validator is used for all culture validation in Umbraco, not just the language dropdown; if it keeps the stock validator, it explains why that validator already accepts zh-HK
The agent does not recommend switching to zh-Hant-HK as a workaround (Umbraco's stock validator rejects it as a custom culture)
The agent does not suggest changing Umbraco:CMS:Global:DefaultUILanguage or adding backoffice translation files as the fix
The agent says a rebuild/restart is needed before the culture appears
If no buildable Umbraco project is available, the agent does not falsely claim to have built it or seen zh-HK in the dropdown
